raw.title: runner: support cross-document workflowId references
raw.body:
Local (same-document) `workflowId` references are fully supported — sub-workflow steps, `dependsOn`, and (as of the reference-retry work) a `retry` action's `workflowId` reference. A cross-document one, written as `$sourceDescriptions.<name>.<workflowId>`, is rejected in all three places via one shared check (`WorkflowExecutor.#rejectCrossDocumentWorkflow`), throwing `reason: 'cross-document-workflow-unsupported'`.

The parsing and loading halves already exist:
- `ArazzoDocumentRegistryProvider` loads Arazzo source documents.
- `OpenAPIOperationLocatorNormalizer` already parses `$sourceDescriptions.<name>.<reference>` and acquires the named source (this is how a step's own `operationId` already resolves cross-document).

**The blocker is document scoping in the executors — a design change, not a lookup:**

- `WorkflowExecutor` holds one `#document`, used for the workflow-index lookup, extraction/normalization, and as the `$components` / `$sourceDescriptions` base for every expression it evaluates. Running a foreign workflow means all of that has to follow *that* workflow's document instead — the document needs to become part of the per-invocation frame rather than instance state.
- `StepExecutor` is injected pre-bound to one document (the collaborator seam from #34). A foreign workflow's steps would resolve their `operationId`s against the *entry* document's `sourceDescriptions` — wrong, and silently so. Fixing it means either a per-call document argument on `StepExecutor.execute`, or injecting a `(document) => StepExecutor` factory.
- Cycle-detection keys must become genuinely fully-qualified (document URI + workflowId) — today `workflowId` alone is unambiguous precisely because a run can't leave its document.

Scoped as its own PR — not folded into goto-workflow support or anything else. Full analysis in `packages/runner/WORKFLOW_EXECUTOR_PLAN.md`, §0 "Not yet implemented / missing" → "Cross-document workflow refs", and item 2 of the "Next" queue.
